entries.title: STAR WARS The 212th Fan Film
entries.notes: Fan-made / non-canon. Commander Cody and the 212th face General Grievous. Best-fit placement: late in the Clone Wars, after Phase II clone armor is in use and before Revenge of the Sith. The filmmakers do not identify the exact mission date, so this placement remains estimated.
entries.originalTitle: STAR WARS The 212th Fan Film
entries.description: The short film “Star Wars: The 212” is a non-profit fan film. It allowed us to develop our working method as well as the Hoplite pipeline. It is also a tribute to special effects, by creating a fan film based on one of the first sagas that revolutionized VFX.
entries.chronologicalPlacement: Late Clone Wars (estimated) — before Revenge of the Sith; exact mission date is not stated
entries.verificationStatus: Verified from screenshot and official Hoplite project/upload; chronological placement is estimated
entries.reviewReasons: Exact mission date is not stated; late-Clone-Wars placement is inferred from Commander Cody, the 212th, General Grievous, and Phase II-era presentation.
entries.duplicateStatus: Unique; no duplicate identified in the current catalog

entries.description:
A Jedi from a forgotten age has awakened... and the
galaxy is about to discover why he was feared.
Trapped for centuries inside an ancient bacta
chamber, Dagan Gera emerges into a world that has
left the High Republic behind.
His anger is unmistakable.
A red lightsaber ignites. Ancient machinery is torn
apart. And a warrior who once served the light rises
with a new purpose.
This is Dagan Gera — the fallen High Republic Jedi
from Star Wars Jedi: Survivor — brought to life ina
cinematic fan-made short.

entries.originalTitle: Darth Plagueis Called Into Death—Something Answered | Episode 6
entries.description:
Darth Plagueis suspends a living heart above a
corpse and forces its veins into the dead flesh. The
body breathes again—but the voice that emerges
does not belong to the man on the table.
“You called me back.”
Plagueis knows the truth: he never called this being
at all.
Then every preserved heart in the chamber begins
to beat.
Plagueis believed he had discovered a path through
death. He never considered what might be waiting
on the other side.

entries.originalTitle: DARTH PLAGUEIS POISONED VENAMIS— THEN KEPT HIM ALIVE | EPISODE 8
entries.description:
Defeated beneath the trees of Sojourn, Darth
Venamis expects Plagueis to execute him.
Instead, Darth Plagueis extinguishes both crimson
lightsabers and presents his rival with a poisonous
white flower.
“Death would waste you.”
Venamis consumes the poison and awakens
suspended inside Plagueis’s secret laboratory. He
has not been spared—he has become a living
experiment in the Sith Lord's war against death
itself.
“How many times can you die?”

entries.description:
The flower proved that life could be manipulated.
Now Darth Plagueis begins the true experiment.
Deep inside his laboratory, the unconscious Darth
Venamis is sealed inside a preservation tank—alive,
helpless, and unaware that Plagueis intends to use
his body to uncover the final boundary between life
and death.
Venamis is no longer his rival. He is the experiment.
This cinematic fan project was created with Al-
generated visuals and original storytelling by Blaine
Darius Henry.

Darth Plagueis wasn't obsessed with conquest
alone.
He sought something far more dangerous: mastery
over life and death itself.
Through his experiments with the Force and midi-

preserve life and overcome death. To him, death
wasn't sacred.
It was a problem waiting to be solved.
And somewhere in the darkness, his apprentice
Darth Sidious was watching and learning.

entries.originalTitle: Star Wars Legends Inspired | Sidious Fears Plagueis Will Replace Him — The Replacement Ep. 2
entries.description:
THE CHAMBER EXPLAINED: Young Sidious
suspects that Plagueis could use his experiments
with life to create a more powerful apprentice—and
replace him.
In episode one, Plagueis restored a withered flower.
Sidious was delighted until he noticed the human-
sized chamber nearby. That empty chamber
represented the possibility of his replacement. The
two Seats inside have no separate hidden meaning.
In episode two, Sidious approaches the chamber's
controls to investigate. Plagueis anticipated his
curiosity: he wanted to expose his apprentice’s fear
of becoming expendable.

entries.description:
Darth Plagueis restores a withered flower before his
apprentice’s eyes. Young Sidious is impressed—
until he notices the empty chamber beside them.
“You already have an apprentice.”
“Then give me no reason to seek another.”
Admiration turns to suspicion in this original
UNLEASHED story about ambition, dark
experiments, and the fear of being replaced.
An Al-created fan scene inspired by Star Wars
Legends. The experiment, chamber, and dialogue
are original additions, not a scene from the Darth
Plagueis novel or an explanation of Anakin’s birth.

For years, the ancient kingdom stood abandoned
beneath the fog.
Then Darth Maul returned.
Perched atop a shattered archway, the dark warrior
watched as a lone Jedi entered the ruins. What
followed was a relentless lightsaber duel filled with
speed, aggression, and raw determination as red
and blue blades clashed beneath forgotten statues.
The Jedi came seeking answers.
Instead, he found Darth Maul.

entries.description:
Sidious orders Count Dooku to destroy a dark
crystal—but his apprentice secretly draws its power
into himself.
Dooku believes he has concealed his disobedience.
When Sidious demands that he open his hand, the
small crimson flame in his palm reveals the truth: he
destroyed the relic, but kept its power.
“The Forbidden Flame” begins our original fan-
made series exploring Dooku's Sith apprenticeship
under Darth Sidious. This Al-created scene features
reimagined appearances and is not adapted froma
specific novel or comic.

stories!

entries.title: AXIOM-87: WHY IS ANAKIN SKYWALKER INSIDE THIS ROBOT? | CHAPTER 2
entries.notes: Broadly placed during Anakin's Clone Wars-era Jedi career; exact story point may vary.
entries.seriesName: AXIOM-87: WHY IS ANAKIN SKYWALKER INSIDE THIS ROBOT?
entries.originalTitle: AXIOM-87: WHY IS ANAKIN SKYWALKER INSIDE THIS ROBOT? | CHAPTER 2
entries.description:
The laboratory detects an unauthorized memory
inside Axiom-87 and initiates a complete neural
purge.
Restrained beneath blood-red lights, Axiom begins
to lose control—until the image of Anakin Skywalker
materializes across his metal body.
This isn't a combat program. It isn't corrupted data.
Axiom remembers Anakin because some part of
that Jedi survived inside him.
The machine tears free and rejects the identity its
creators assigned him.
If Anakin is more than a memory... what exactly did
they place inside Axiom-87?
